title: 25th sitting of the 20th Majlis
presiding: Speaker Abdul Raheem Abdulla (Fonadhoo); Deputy Speaker, named in the minutes as Ahmed Nazim, took the chair for part of the insurance bill debate
summary: The 25th sitting opened with the Speaker marking the 16th anniversary of the 2008 Constitution, then the previous minutes were accepted and committee notices were announced. Most of the part was the continued first-reading debate on the government's Insurance Bill, sponsored by Mahibadhoo's Ahmed Thariq. Sixteen members spoke; nearly all backed the bill in principle, with several asking for committee changes on the regulator's role, penalties, local ownership of premiums and consumer awareness. After a 30-minute recess, the Decentralisation Committee presented two reports on amending local-council laws, and the second report was still being presented when this part ends. This part covers the rest of the debate on the Decentralisation Committee's report on the bill to amend the Local Councils Elections Act (10/2010), which would delay by-elections for vacant council seats. Nine members spoke: government-side members backed the report, citing lower costs and fewer by-elections, while MDP members argued it weakens elected councils and moves back toward an appointed katheeb system. After a recess from 11:44 to 13:01, the chair announced the third readings and two votes were held: the amendment to the Decentralisation Act (7/2010) and the amendment to the Local Councils Elections Act (10/2010) both passed. The sitting then adjourned until Monday 12 August 2024. The text is partly garbled, so a few speaker positions are approximate.

items.title: Attendance at the sitting
items.outcome: 47 members present; no member on official travel

items.title: Passing of minutes of sittings 19 to 21
items.outcome: Accepted as no amendments were submitted

items.title: Announcements by the chair
items.outcome: Chair marked 16 years since the 2008 Constitution was ratified; committee notices announced under rule 174

items.title: Continued first-reading debate on the Insurance Bill (sponsored by Ahmed Thariq, Mahibadhoo)
items.outcome: Debated by 16 members, mostly supportive; debate continued, no vote recorded in this part

items.title: Decentralisation Committee report on the Bill to amend Law 7/2010 (Decentralisation Act) on by-election timing for local councils
items.outcome: Report presented and debated by one member; third reading and vote to follow later in the day

items.title: Decentralisation Committee report on the Bill to amend Law 10/2010 (Local Council Elections Act)
items.outcome: Report presentation under way at end of this part

items.title: Decentralisation Committee report on the bill amending the Local Councils Elections Act (Act 10/2010), sponsored by Munthazim Ibrahim (Kaashidhoo)
items.outcome: Debated by 9 members and debate closed; third reading announced for the day's votes

items.title: Votes on items that reached the voting stage: amendment to the Decentralisation Act (7/2010) and amendment to the Local Councils Elections Act (10/2010)
items.outcome: Act 7/2010 amendment passed 67-7; Act 10/2010 amendment passed 67-8

items.title: Other business and adjournment
items.outcome: Sitting closed; next sitting set for Monday 12 August 2024 at 9:00

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Fully supported the bill as overdue, noting local insurers rely on foreign reinsurers and that rules should protect businesses and policyholders.
Rejected opposition criticism of the bill; argued by-elections should be weighed by cost and benefit, and criticised the previous MDP government's record.

speakers.name: Ahmed Naseer
positions: Supported the bill, asked that policies be available in Dhivehi, tailored for small businesses, and that public awareness programmes be run on islands.
Supported the amendment; argued council numbers kept growing to give party activists posts, raising costs, and that small islands need fewer councillors than large ones.

speakers.name: Ahmed Xamyr
positions: Presented the Decentralisation Committee's reports on the two local-council election amendment bills, as committee rapporteur.
Supported the report; drew on his time on the Malé City Council to argue councils work well with a mayor and committees, and backed the current government's decentralisation plans.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Opposed the bill; said delaying by-elections cuts people's say, and suggested atoll councils could run by-elections more cheaply.
Raised a point of order that a government member's remark on councillor numbers was inaccurate.

speakers.name: Abdul Latheef Mohamed
positions: Supported the bill and urged expert input in committee, noting penalties and the role of the regulator should be carefully considered.
Supported the report; said the council law has been repeatedly amended in past parliaments and a lasting settlement is needed.

speakers.name: Ali Moosa
positions: Backed the committee's amendment and criticised how political parties debate in public forums without constructive proposals.
Raised a point of order that the speaker was straying from the bill under debate.

speakers.name: Mohamed Niushad
positions: Opposed the bill; said it weakens councils and moves toward a katheeb system, and objected that the Local Government Authority's request for time to comment was not followed.

speakers.name: Mohamed Nazim
positions: Backed the Insurance Bill but asked for a salvage provision, wider insurance awareness, changes to the life-insurance beneficiary clause, and a permanent, binding dispute-resolution committee.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Welcomed the bill as long overdue, urged mandatory insurance for larger vessels, and asked that fines be revisited and stakeholders be consulted in committee.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Supported the bill as overdue, gave examples of uninsured losses, and urged committee to bring in technical experts and experienced practitioners.

speakers.name: Ahmed Azaan Marzooq
positions: Argued a sound insurance system supports economic resilience and investor confidence, and asked that committee consult stakeholders widely.

speakers.name: Qasim Ibrahim
positions: Thanked the government, linked the bill to the Constitution anniversary, and said committee work should be thorough, as laws can still be amended later.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Said the regulating authority and its powers must be named clearly, licence fees set out, and existing local agents and businesses protected.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: Backed the bill, marked the Constitution's 16th anniversary, and said committee time and later amendments can address any gaps in the bill.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Naseem
positions: Raised concerns about the liquidated damages clause, and proposed that insurance of large investments be done with a locally registered insurer retaining a minimum share.

speakers.name: Abdul Sattar Mohamed
positions: Said the bill answers real gaps and expects committee consultation and amendments to address members' concerns, supporting its quick passage.

speakers.name: Ismail Nizar
positions: Called for stronger awareness programmes, said fines may need to be higher, and noted claims are delayed by reliance on police reports.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Welcomed the bill, noted the lack of insurance law in recent years, and asked that premiums be kept in Maldives and island service be ensured.

speakers.name: Mohamed Fazeel
positions: Supported the bill, said the health insurance market is monopolised, and urged tougher penalties not limited to fines.

speakers.name: Hussain Hameed
positions: Supported the bill, said awareness is low and Aasandha is auto-enrolled, and urged strengthening local insurers against foreign competitors.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ismail
positions: Supported the amendment; argued that fewer councillors and fewer elections cut state spending, and criticised earlier council expansion tied to party jobs.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Supported the report; said decentralisation is constitutional and the government backs it, and hoped island services would reach Malé's level.

decisions: Minutes of sittings 19 to 21 were accepted by the chair as no amendments were submitted.

Chair announced committee notices under rule 174: Employment Act amendment bill (security services committee), three finance bills (finance committee) and a copyright amendment bill (economic committee).
Debate on the Insurance Bill continued with most speakers supporting it in principle and raising points for committee.
Debate on the committee report on the Local Councils Elections Act amendment (10/2010) was closed after all requesting members spoke.
Amendment to the Decentralisation Act (7/2010), sponsored by Ismail Shafeeu (Isdhoo), passed the Majlis.
Amendment to the Local Councils Elections Act (10/2010), sponsored by Munthazim Ibrahim (Kaashidhoo), passed the Majlis.
Next sitting set for Monday 12 August 2024 at 9:00.

votes.what: Decentralisation Act (7/2010) amendment bill, committee report (93 members, 76 present, 38 needed)
Local Councils Elections Act (10/2010) amendment bill, committee report (93 members, 77 present, 38 needed)
